newsitem.title: UK: NWE oil products dip, Antwerp fuel trades at $79.5.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products dip, Antwerp fuel trades at $79.5.

text.p: NWE oil products were steady to softer on Monday but business was largely killed off by public holidays in the U.K. and the U.S., traders said.

High sulphur fuel oil barges were weaker and around 6,000 tonnes changed hands at $79.50 fob Antwerp. This was marginally weaker than Friday's levels, although traders did not cite any special reasons for the softness. No trade was heard done in Rotterdam.
Many dealers are wary of burgeoning Russian exports, which are expected to gather pace as summer unfolds.

Gasoline was steady to slightly weaker but very thin. British newspapers said over the weekend that they expected a delay of two or three weeks to the new government's first post-election budget, which is expected to include gasoline tax increases and has already led to some hoarding of duty-paid gasoline.
The Treasury said on Sunday that British Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Gordon Brown will announce the date of his first budget shortly after parliament returns on June 2.
Traders expected the delay to be bearish for the prompt period and to flatten the backwardation between June and July.

"There is no point stockpiling it now and paying for tankage if it is going to sit there for a few more weeks," one refinery-based trader said. "So I expect to see a little more selling in the short term."
No trades were heard done and dealers expected the market to have softened slightly from Eurograde business concluded late on Friday at $212 fob ARA.
Gas oil was also lacklustre and premiums to the June IPE contract, which was closed on Monday for the holiday, were steady.
Dealers expected arbitrage opportunities from the Mediterranean to keep a cap on prices for the moment.
